To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the liver weight and the fractional clearance of colloidal particles are normal in rats with total arterialization of the portal vein; 2) in rats with total portal arterialization, the concentration and activity of hepatic microsomes are significantly lower than in control animals; 3) the same findings are obtained after treatment of rats with portacavel shunt and arterialization of the stump with phenobarbital.

1) the hepatic blood flow is normal after arterialization of the stump of the portal trunk in rats with portocaval anastomosis, and 2) the cytochrome p-450 content of hepatic microsomes is lower than in normal rats, even after phenobarbital induction.
total arterialization of the portal vein does not prevent the decrease of cytochrome P450 in rats with shunt.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of portacaval anastomosis on the liver.
the effects of portacaval shunting on liver function.
the effect of portacaval shunting and portal arterialization of the rat liver on hepatic cytoplasmic and mitochondrial enzymes and on the hepatic microcirculation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
hepatic arterialization of the stump of the portal trunk in portacaval shunted rats does not restore the normal hepatic cyto-chrome P-450 level.
the portal arterialization is a useful procedure to maintain the hepatic blood flow, but it has no effect on the hepatic cyto- chrome P-450.
hepatic arterialization does not restore the hepatic microsome activity in rats with portocaval shunts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
portacaval shunts with or without portal arterialization are able to reduce liver size and cytochrome P 450 level.
in portacaval shunted rats, arterialization of the portal vein is not able to prevent a decrease of cytochrome P 450 concentration.
portacaval shunting of the portal blood flow is not a simple process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can use the liver for the purpose of removing toxins from the blood and that this is a safe and effective way to do so.
the hepatic blood flow is not the main determinant for a normal activity of hepatic microsomes.
the liver is a very important organ, but it is also very delicate and can be easily damaged.
